citations.H40.013: The Tabular List titles subcategory H40.0 'Glaucoma suspect' and code H40.01 'Open angle with borderline findings, low risk'. ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I: the conventions and instructions of the classification take precedence over guidelines. Section IV.H: do not code diagnoses documented as 'suspected' or with similar terms indicating uncertainty; code the condition to the highest degree of certainty for the visit. Section I.A.9.b: codes titled 'unspecified' are for use when the information in the medical record is insufficient to assign a more specific code. Here the ophthalmologist's assessment is 'glaucoma suspect, both eyes: open angle with borderline findings, low risk'. That is not an uncertain statement about glaucoma: it names a condition for which the classification has its own subcategory, and the words of the assessment are the title of the code. Glaucoma itself is not diagnosed and is not coded. The code for both eyes is assigned.

coder_notes: Counter-case: the more specific code is the supported one. The word 'suspect' does not make this an uncertain diagnosis; compare a 'suspected' infection, which is not coded. Preglaucoma, unspecified (H40.003) would leave out the type that the provider states. The provider states every part of the code: the coder counts no risk factors and infers no angle status. The cup-to-disc ratio, the pressures and the open angles are the findings behind the diagnosis and are not coded beside it (Section I.B.5). The visual fields and the imaging are normal. This is a visit for a current condition under observation, so neither a routine examination code nor a follow-up examination code applies. A family history of glaucoma is denied.
